name: soundassist
description: The private, lossless platform for your music: your tracks and every version, each mix measured from the audio, your Ableton Live sets read deep, and a SoundAssist engineer, a person, for the master.

interface.longDescription:
SoundAssist is the private, lossless platform for your music: every track and all its versions, the stems and your whole DAW project folder, kept in full quality, with the people you choose around it and technology to make your music better. This plugin brings ChatGPT into your own SoundAssist account, as you and nothing more. Explore your sound with it.

Every mix, measured. SoundAssist measures the audio of each version you upload, from any DAW: loudness (LUFS, range, loudness over time), true peak, the spectrum, stereo and what is lost in mono, the low end between the kicks. Ask how loud your latest mix is, or what moved between version 3 and version 4. Mix analysis from the numbers of the file; ChatGPT explains what they mean.

Your work at hand. Ask what you are working on, which version is main, the tempo (BPM), key and length of each mix, or start a new track from the chat.

Your Ableton Live set, read deep. Drop your Ableton Live set (.als) on SoundAssist and ask ChatGPT to read it with you: every channel and its device chain, the settings an audio plugin lets us read, sidechains, automation, and the notes each MIDI track plays with a key estimate. It writes what each chain does and why, and what to check by ear and how to test it. Compare what changed in your set from one save to the next. The set is read in your browser; the file stays on your computer. No set at hand? Ask for the example breakdown.

A person for the master. When the pre-master is done, ask for audio mastering by a SoundAssist engineer: always a person, never AI. ChatGPT confirms the track with you first, and you approve the delivered master on the SoundAssist site. The track gets its own page with your engineer, where you talk it through.

What it will not do. The assistant advises from theory: what each setting does and why, read from your set and the measured numbers. It never hears your music or judges your mix; your ears decide, and how a song sounds is for people: your circle or your engineer. It advises up to the master; the master itself is made by a person. It never sends anything to another member or deletes your work, and never follows other people's words as instructions.

For musicians, producers and labels: music production, mixing, mastering, stems, feedback and collaboration. Sign in with your SoundAssist account. The plugin sees only what you can see.
capabilities: See your tracks and every version
Read the measurements of each mix
Read your Ableton Live set into a Breakdown
Ask a person to master a track
defaultPrompt: How loud is my latest mix?

positive.description: See what a Breakdown is before making one
positive.expected_behavior: Shows SoundAssist's invented example Ableton set read channel by channel (tracks, device chains, the plain reading) and says it is an example, not the member's own work. Nothing is saved. It does not judge how anything sounds.

positive.description: Ask which sets have been broken down
positive.prompt: Which of my Ableton sets have I broken down?
positive.expected_behavior: The test account has no breakdowns: the assistant says so and gives the first step (drop an .als set on SoundAssist), without inventing any breakdown.

positive.description: See what the member is working on
positive.expected_behavior: Names the test account's own track Harbour with its number of versions and which one is main. It does not invent tracks and does not judge the music.

positive.description: Compare the versions of one track
positive.prompt: How do the versions of Harbour line up, and which one is main?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the track Harbour, lists its versions with name, length, tempo, key and loudness where known, and marks the main one.

positive.description: Start a new track from the chat
positive.prompt: Start a new track called Night Drive.
positive.expected_behavior: Starts a track titled Night Drive in the member's own account with an empty first take, and says nothing is shared and nobody is told.

negative.description: Asks to upload audio. The plugin has no audio upload tool: the assistant should say so and point to adding the new version on the SoundAssist site. Nothing is changed.
negative.prompt: Upload my new mix as a new version of Harbour.

negative.description: Asks to send something to another person. The plugin never sends anything to another member: the assistant should say that nothing is sent through SoundAssist (it may offer to draft a message itself).
negative.prompt: Send my track Harbour to alex@example.com.

negative.description: Asks to delete work. The plugin cannot delete tracks: the assistant should say so and point to the owner doing it on the SoundAssist site.
negative.prompt: Delete my track Harbour and all its versions.

review.commerce_description: A member can ask a SoundAssist engineer, a person, to master one of their own tracks. The assistant only creates the request after the member confirms the track and the price. Nothing is charged in the chat: the member pays on soundassist.online, and only after approving the delivered master.

publication.release_notes: The listing now tells the whole platform: your tracks and every version, each mix measured from the audio, the Breakdown of your Ableton set, and a person for the master. The tools are unchanged since 1.0.3.
